communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All incident reports, call logs, computer-aided dispatch (CAD) records, and related documentation from January 1, 2020 to the present reflecting calls for service that were identified as, or subsequently determined to be, initiated by a voice-activated device, virtual assistant, or AI-enabled emergency feature, including but not limited to Apple Siri, Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Samsung Bixby, or device-based emergency detection features such as Apple crash detection, fall detection, or Emergency SOS.

All incident reports, call logs, and related documentation from January 1, 2020 to the present reflecting calls for service categorized as accidental, unintentional, pocket dial, abandoned, or device-generated, where responding officers noted or documented that the call originated from a smart device or voice-activated assistant.

Any internal policies, directives, training materials, bulletins, or guidance documents related to responding to or handling calls originating from voice-activated devices, virtual assistants, or AI-enabled emergency features on smart devices.

Any communications, including emails, memos, or internal reports, discussing accidental or unintentional 911 calls generated by AI, smart devices or voice assistants.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Steven Catron (Flora Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Steven Catron (6303-1830)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

title: Pete Sumalo Montejo ICE Death Report

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Pete Sumalo Montejo ICE Death Report
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. The ICE Detainee Death Report for Pete Sumalo Montejo, who passed away December 5, 2025, in ICE custody in Texas. 
2. A copy of the ICE ERO or IHSC Significant Incident Report or Significant Event Notification

According to the information currently published on ICE's website, ICE was under a Congressional mandate to release this information no later than 30 days after his death, and to update it no more than 60 days after each immigrant's death. ICE has released a Death Report for Jean Wilson Brutus and Shiraz Sachwani, both of whom died after Mr. Sumalo Montejo. 

I make this request under both 5 USC 552(a)(2) - which governs the agency's affirmative disclosure obligations - and 552(a)(3), which concerns the agency's obligation to respond to a request. 

Pursuant to 6 C.F.R. 5.5(e)(1)(ii) and (iv), I seek expedited processing of this request, and certify and attest under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 USC 1746 that the following statements are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and current understanding: 

1. I am a member of the media, primarily engaged information dissemination. See www.MuckRack.com/Andrew-Free.

2. I research and publish regarding deaths in ICE custody. My work documenting deaths in ICE detention is published, cited, and relied upon by national media outlets, including the Washington Post, the New York Times, the L.A. Times, and others. 

3. As of the date of filing my filing of this request, ICE has not posted its Detainee Death Report for this individual. 

4. There is an urgent need to inform the public about the circumstances ICE is aware of surrounding this death. Congress is currently contemplating alterations to DHS and ICE's funding, and the facts of each death in custody directly impact demands lawmakers and the public may wish to press when authorizing future funding increases, or applying limits to them.

5. Deaths in ICE custody reached their highest numbers in 20 years in 2025, and they have been the subject of widespread media coverage, and there is significant reason to believe ICE's treatment of people in detention has not met the standards it claims it adheres to when defending its actions in public statements. This coverage has prompted a number of responses by DHS's Twitter page and other public statements, pushing back against the coverage.

6. I will make the records available to the general public upon receiving them.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

communications.subject: ICE FOIA 2026-ICFO-16837
communications.communication:
06/09/2026 

Andrew  Free 
MuckRock News, DEPT MR204566 
Boston, Massachusetts 02115 

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2026-ICFO-16837 
 
Dear Requester: 

This acknowledges receipt of your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), dated 2/11/2026, and to your request for expedited treatment. Your request was received in this office on 2/11/2026. Specifically, you requested records for Pete Sumalo Montejo. 

Your request for expedited treatment is hereby denied. 

Under the DHS FOIA regulations, expedited processing of a FOIA request is warranted if the request involves “circumstances in which the lack of expedited treatment could reasonably be expected to pose an imminent threat to the life or physical safety of an individual,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1)(i), or “an urgency to inform the public about an actual or alleged federal government activity, if made by a person primarily engaged in disseminating information,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(l)(ii).  Requesters seeking expedited processing must submit a statement explaining in detail the basis for the request, and that statement must be certified by the requester to be true and correct.  6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(3). 

Your request for expedited processing is denied because you do not qualify for either category under 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1).   You have not established that lack of expedited treatment in this case will pose an imminent threat to the life or physical safety of an individual.  While you may be primarily engaged in the dissemination of information, you have not detailed with specificity why you feel there is an urgency to inform the public about Pete Sumalo Montejo.  Qualifying urgency would need to exceed the public’s right to know about government activity generally.  You also did not offer sufficient supporting evidence of an interest of the public greater than the public’s general interest in Pete Sumalo Montejo.  Your letter was conclusory in nature and did not present any facts to justify a grant of expedited processing under the applicable standards. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10- day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you care to narrow the scope of your request, please contact our office. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 

Provisions of the FOIA allow us to recover part of the cost of complying with your request.  We shall charge you for records in accordance with the DHS Interim FOIA regulations, as they apply to media requesters.  As a media requester, you will be charged 10 cents per page for duplication; the first 100 pages are free.  We will construe the submission of your request as an agreement to pay up to $25.00. You will be contacted before any further fees are accrued. 

If you deem the decision to deny expedited treatment of your request an adverse determination, you have the right to appeal.  Should you wish to do so, you must send your appeal and a copy of this letter, within 90 days of the date of this letter following the procedures outlined in the DHS FOIA regulations at 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.5(e)(2). You may submit your appeal electronically through the SecureRelease Portal (preferred) or via regular mail to: 

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Office of the Principal Legal Advisor 
U.S. Department of Homeland Security 
500 12th Street,, S.W., Mail Stop 5900 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5900 

Your envelope and letter should be marked “FOIA Appeal.”  Copies of the FOIA and DHS regulations are available at www.dhs.gov/foia. 

ICE has queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request. 

If you have any questions, please contact the FOIA office or FOIA Public Liaison at ICEFOIAPublicLiaison@ice.dhs.gov or (866) 633-1182. Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448. 

Your request has been assigned tracking number 2026-ICFO-16837. Please use this number in future correspondence. 

Sincerely, 

ICE FOIA Office 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Freedom of Information Act Office 
500 12th Street, S.W., Stop 5009 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5009

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2026-ICAP-00465 
 
Dear Requester: 

This is the final response to your 6/10/2026, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) appeal to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), for records pertaining Pete Sumalo Montejo.  Your request was received in this office on 6/26/2026. 

This is to inform you that we are administratively closing your request regarding the expedited processing denial, as the denial was affirmed by GILD. Please be advised that your original request will continue to be processed under 2026-ICFO-16837. 

Additionally, your original request has been assigned to a processor and is moving forward in accordance with standard procedures. 

This letter advises you that we have administratively closed your request file, and no fees will be assessed. 

Please refer to your original request reference number 2026-ICFO-16837 for future inquiries or any future correspondence. If you have any questions please contact the ICE FOIA Public Liaison at ICEFOIAPublicLiaison@ice.dhs.gov or (866) 633-1182. 

Sincerely, 

ICE FOIA Office 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Freedom of Information Act Office 
500 12th Street, S.W., Stop 5009 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5009

Andrew  Free 
MuckRock News, DEPT MR204566 
263 Huntington Ave 
Boston, Massachusetts 02115 

RE: ICE FOIA Request 2026-ICFO-16837 
Dear Requester: 
This letter is in response to your status inquiry regarding your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), in which you requested: records for Pete Sumalo Montejo. 

As of today, your request has been assigned to a processor and is currently under review. If responsive records have been located, they will be reviewed to determine whether they may be released. 

ICE FOIA processes requests in the order they are received, on a first-in, first-out basis. We apologize for the delay in the processing of your request. Please be assured that a processor in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request. 

If you have any questions, please contact the FOIA Public Liaison at ICEFOIAPublicLiaison@ice.dhs.gov or (866) 633-1182. Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448. 

Your request has been assigned reference number 2026-ICFO-16837. Please include this number in any future correspondence regarding your request. 

Sincerely, 

Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Office 
Office of Information Governance and Privacy 
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) 
ICE-FOIA@ice.dhs.gov | www.ice.gov/foia
